newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil poll shows gov't popularity up to 28.7 pct.
newsitem.headline: Brazil poll shows gov't popularity up to 28.7 pct.

text.p: The popularity of the Brazilian government is on the increase, but the number of people who give it the thumbs-up are still a minority, according to a poll published Sunday by magazine Isto E.
The percentage of respondents who considered the government to be doing a "good" or "excellent" job rose to 28.7 percent from 17.8 percent in June, Isto E said.
Those who considered the goverment "bad" or "awful" fell to 32.5 percent from 39.1 percent while 38.8 percent considered it "OK", down from 41 percent.

The poll, by market research firm Brasmarket, coincides with an upturn in the popularity of candidates from President Fernando Henrique Cardoso's Brazilian Social Democractic Party who are standing in upcoming municipal elections, Isto E said.
